$comment: Machine-readable fork ownership record. See scripts/workflowleaf/README.md.

allowedUpstreamEdits.purpose: Regenerated by pnpm when the WorkflowLeaf packages join the workspace.
allowedUpstreamEdits.removeWhen: WorkflowLeaf packages are removed from the workspace.

allowedUpstreamEdits.purpose: One @import line so every agent in this repository is told the fork stays additive, without having to find scripts/workflowleaf/. AGENTS.md was the alternative and changes far more often upstream.
allowedUpstreamEdits.removeWhen: WorkflowLeaf is removed from the repository, or Claude Code gains a project instruction source that upstream does not own.

orientation.reason: Onboarding material that lies is worse than none. A commit that moves the domain shape, the CLI commands, the profile schema, which executors exist, or these rules must say so in the orientation, or say in its message why it did not.

enablement.reason: Conformance case C14: deleting the WorkflowLeaf packages must leave T3 building. No upstream manifest may depend on one, and no allow-listed upstream edit may import one. Sharpen this when a host binding lands under apps/server/src/workflowleaf/.

importBoundaries.reason: Core stays portable: no T3 types, no filesystem, no environment, no ambient clock. Digests and timestamps are inputs, not side effects.

Only the T3 adapter may know that T3 exists. The one exception is @t3tools/shared/nodeSqliteClient, a generic node:sqlite port of the Effect SQL client with no T3 domain in it; the plan says to reuse the repository's SQLite conventions rather than vendor a second copy.
